subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

If the allegations were substantiated (1)/ and procedural lapses proven, the committee might have (2)/ had enough reason to initiate an internal probe (3)/ which never occurred. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence attempts to form a **mixed conditional** structure.
 
• “If the allegations were substantiated” uses **past simple**, suggesting a second conditional structure.
 
• However, the main clause uses **“might have had”**, which reflects a third conditional structure.
 
• For correct parallelism, it should be either **“were substantiated… might have had”** (mixed conditional with clear logic) or **“had been substantiated… might have had”** (third conditional). The inconsistency makes part (2) structurally incorrect in context.

Correct sentence: *If the allegations **had been substantiated** and procedural lapses proven, the committee might have had enough reason to initiate an internal probe which never occurred.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Conditional:** If + past simple, would/might + base verb (hypothetical present).
 
• **Third Conditional:** If + past perfect, would/might have + past participle (unreal past).
 
• Consistency between the if-clause and main clause is necessary for grammatical accuracy.
